title: Anthropic opens Enterprise Frontier Safeguards to public beta — misuse monitoring without data retention
subtitle: EFS lets Claude Enterprise customers keep prompts and responses in their own cloud while Anthropic scans across requests for coordinated misuse patterns. Bridgewater, Salesforce, and Stripe are design partners.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic moved Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) from private to public beta on November 23. EFS is available through the Claude Platform directly, the Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, and Claude on Google Cloud. It targets a specific gap: enterprises that need zero-data-retention compliance usually lose Anthropic's misuse monitoring in the bargain. EFS splits the work — customers host the prompts and responses in their own storage, and Anthropic's monitoring reads across many requests to detect coordinated misuse that any single request would hide. Anthropic charges nothing for the service.

The novel capability is cross-request detection. Most policy enforcement on frontier models judges each prompt alone, which misses a user who distributes a bad task across twenty seemingly innocent prompts. EFS looks for patterns across the sequence. Private-beta design partners include Bridgewater, Salesforce, and Stripe — organizations with significant compliance constraints that would otherwise keep them away from managed monitoring. More than 100 customers contributed to the beta.

The product tracks the regulatory shift Anthropic has been chasing all year. California's SB-53 safety framework and the EU AI Office's systemic-risk requirements both assume frontier providers can monitor misuse even when they can't retain content. EFS is the first production answer to that requirement that doesn't force customers to give up data control. It is still beta, settings can change, and HIPAA-ready organizations aren't eligible yet.

A note for learners: 'zero data retention' and 'misuse monitoring' used to be in direct tension because both features relied on the same data. EFS shows one way out — move the storage to the customer and move the monitoring to a stream Anthropic sees without keeping. If you're ever asked to design a policy system for a regulated workload, that split is a pattern worth stealing: separate the data custodian from the compliance scanner, and give each the minimum it needs.
